name: Docker
discovers: Discover Docker containers and the services they expose.
summary: Discover Docker containers and the services they expose. Supports proxy and socket.

transports.name: Proxy
transports.description: Connects over TCP, optionally with TLS.

fields.label: Docker API Port
fields.help_text: Docker API port. Use 2375 for non-TLS proxies (Tecnativa, HAProxy) or 2376 for TLS.

fields.label: URL Path Prefix
fields.help_text: Optional URL path prefix appended after the port

fields.label: SSL Certificate
fields.help_text: PEM-encoded client certificate. All three TLS fields (cert, key, CA chain) must be provided together.

fields.label: SSL Private Key
fields.help_text: PEM private key. All three TLS fields must be provided together.

fields.label: SSL CA Chain
fields.help_text: PEM-encoded CA certificate chain. All three TLS fields must be provided together.

transports.name: Socket
transports.description: Connects via the daemon's local socket.

fields.label: Socket Path
fields.help_text: The Docker socket on Unix, or its named pipe on Windows. Leave blank to auto-detect (DOCKER_HOST or /var/run/docker.sock on Unix, the docker_engine pipe on Windows).

name: Instant On
discovers: Discover Instant On switches, access points and gateways, their ports, the uplinks between them, and the MACs attached to each port.
summary: Discover Instant On switches, access points and gateways, their ports, the uplinks between them, and the MACs attached to each port. Supports portal account.

transports.name: Portal Account
transports.description: Connects to the Instant On cloud portal with a site account.

fields.label: Portal Account
fields.help_text: Email address of an Instant On portal account with access to the site. Add a dedicated account with the read-only Viewer role (Site management → Accounts managing this site) rather than using your own administrator login, and make sure multi-factor authentication is disabled on it — the sign-in cannot answer an MFA prompt.

fields.label: Password
fields.help_text: Password for that portal account.

fields.label: Site
fields.help_text: Limit the fetch to one Instant On site by name. Leave blank to read every site this account can see. Assign this credential to a single switch — each host it is assigned to fetches the whole site again.

name: Podman
discovers: Discover Podman containers and the services they expose.
summary: Discover Podman containers and the services they expose. Supports proxy and socket.

transports.name: Proxy
transports.description: Connects over TCP, optionally with TLS.

fields.label: Podman API Port
fields.help_text: Podman API port. Point at a TCP-exposed Podman service (e.g. `podman system service tcp:`) directly or behind a TLS proxy.

fields.label: URL Path Prefix
fields.help_text: Optional URL path prefix appended after the port

fields.label: SSL Certificate
fields.help_text: PEM-encoded client certificate. All three TLS fields (cert, key, CA chain) must be provided together.

fields.label: SSL Private Key
fields.help_text: PEM private key. All three TLS fields must be provided together.

fields.label: SSL CA Chain
fields.help_text: PEM-encoded CA certificate chain. All three TLS fields must be provided together.

transports.name: Socket
transports.description: Connects via the daemon's local socket.

fields.label: Socket Path
fields.help_text: The Podman socket on Unix, or Podman machine's named pipe on Windows. Leave blank to auto-detect (CONTAINER_HOST, then the rootful and rootless sockets on Unix or the podman-machine-default pipe on Windows).

name: SNMP
discovers: Discover a host's interfaces, system details, and CDP/LLDP neighbors.
summary: Discover a host's interfaces, system details, and CDP/LLDP neighbors. Supports v1, v2c, and v3.

fields.label: Community String
fields.help_text: Custom SNMP community string. The default 'public' community is always tried automatically during scans. On Cisco switches, append '@' and a VLAN id — for example 'readonly@20' — to read that VLAN's MAC-address table, which the plain community does not return.

fields.label: Community String
fields.help_text: Custom SNMP community string. The default 'public' community is always tried automatically during scans. On Cisco switches, append '@' and a VLAN id — for example 'readonly@20' — to read that VLAN's MAC-address table, which the plain community does not return.

fields.label: Security Name
fields.help_text: SNMPv3 USM user name (security name).

fields.label: Auth Protocol
fields.help_text: Authentication hash algorithm.

fields.label: Auth Password
fields.help_text: Authentication password (minimum 8 characters).

fields.label: Privacy Protocol
fields.help_text: Privacy (encryption) algorithm.

fields.label: Privacy Password
fields.help_text: Privacy (encryption) password (minimum 8 characters).

fields.label: Context Name
fields.help_text: Optional SNMPv3 context name, applied to bridge and VLAN queries only. Cisco and some other vendors keep a separate MAC-address table per VLAN in a named context; naming it here reads that table instead of the near-empty default one. Interface, LLDP and ARP data always come from the default context.

name: SSH
discovers: Run your own script on a host and record the system details and interfaces it reports.
summary: Run your own script on a host and record the system details and interfaces it reports. Supports key and password.

transports.name: Key
transports.description: Connects over SSH with a private key.

fields.label: Username
fields.help_text: Account the script runs as. Use a dedicated account with only the access the script needs.

fields.label: Private Key
fields.help_text: OpenSSH (ssh-keygen's default) or PEM private key whose public key is in the account's authorized_keys.

fields.label: Key Passphrase
fields.help_text: Only if the private key is encrypted.

fields.label: Scanned Host OS
fields.help_text: Sets how the script runs, in the login shell on Linux, macOS and BSD or in PowerShell on Windows, and the path format for a file on the scanned host.

fields.label: Script
fields.help_text: Runs at each scan. Must print one JSON object of host fields.

fields.label: Timeout (seconds)
fields.help_text: The script is stopped and the run reports a failure after this long.

fields.label: Host Key Fingerprint
fields.help_text: Leave blank to trust the key each host presents the first time and refuse it if it later changes. Enter a fingerprint (ssh-keygen -lf) to require that key instead.

transports.name: Password
transports.description: Connects over SSH with a username and password.

fields.label: Username
fields.help_text: Account the script runs as. Use a dedicated account with only the access the script needs.

fields.label: Password
fields.help_text: Password for that account. The server must allow password authentication.

fields.label: Scanned Host OS
fields.help_text: Sets how the script runs, in the login shell on Linux, macOS and BSD or in PowerShell on Windows, and the path format for a file on the scanned host.

fields.label: Script
fields.help_text: Runs at each scan. Must print one JSON object of host fields.

fields.label: Timeout (seconds)
fields.help_text: The script is stopped and the run reports a failure after this long.

fields.label: Host Key Fingerprint
fields.help_text: Leave blank to trust the key each host presents the first time and refuse it if it later changes. Enter a fingerprint (ssh-keygen -lf) to require that key instead.

name: UniFi Controller
discovers: Discover UniFi-managed switches, access points and gateways, their ports, and the LLDP neighbors and uplinks the controller sees.
summary: Discover UniFi-managed switches, access points and gateways, their ports, and the LLDP neighbors and uplinks the controller sees. Supports api key and local admin.

transports.name: API Key
transports.description: Connects with a controller API key. Requires UniFi OS; the legacy self-hosted Network Application does not support API keys.

fields.label: Controller Port
fields.help_text: 443 for a UniFi OS console (Dream Machine, Cloud Key, Cloud Gateway), 11443 for a self-hosted UniFi OS Server, or 8443 for the legacy self-hosted Network Application. Check the port in your controller's URL — the wrong port fails to connect.

fields.label: Site
fields.help_text: Internal site name, taken from the controller URL (/manage/site/<name>) — not the site's display name. Most installations use 'default'.

fields.label: API Key
fields.help_text: Network Application API key (Settings → Control Plane → Integrations → Create API Key). Requires UniFi OS; the legacy self-hosted Network Application on 8443 has no API keys — use a UniFi Local Admin credential there instead.

transports.name: Local Admin
transports.description: Connects with a local admin account. Works with every controller, including the legacy self-hosted Network Application.

fields.label: Controller Port
fields.help_text: 443 for a UniFi OS console (Dream Machine, Cloud Key, Cloud Gateway), 11443 for a self-hosted UniFi OS Server, or 8443 for the legacy self-hosted Network Application. Check the port in your controller's URL — the wrong port fails to connect.

fields.label: Site
fields.help_text: Internal site name, taken from the controller URL (/manage/site/<name>) — not the site's display name. Most installations use 'default'.

fields.label: Username
fields.help_text: Controller admin username. Use a local-only admin account so multi-factor authentication does not block the login.

fields.label: Password
fields.help_text: Password for the local admin account.

name: Wake-on-LAN
discovers: Wake sleeping hosts before a scan so they are discovered.
summary: Wake sleeping hosts before a scan so they are discovered. Supports magic packet.

transports.name: Magic Packet
transports.description: Sends a magic packet over UDP. The daemon must be on the host's network segment, or the router must forward directed broadcasts or relay the packet.

fields.label: UDP Port
fields.help_text: Most network cards accept the packet on any port. Change it only if a router relay rule listens on another port, commonly 7.

fields.label: Broadcast Address
fields.help_text: Leave blank to send to the broadcast address of each host's subnet, which reaches it when the daemon is on the same network segment or the router forwards directed broadcasts. Otherwise enter where to send it instead: a router address with a relay rule, a Wake-on-LAN relay device, or 255.255.255.255.

fields.label: Wait (seconds)
fields.help_text: How long the daemon waits after sending the packets before the scan starts. Hosts the scan finds count as woken. Allow for disks spinning up and services starting.

fields.label: SecureOn Password
fields.help_text: Only for network cards configured to require one. Six bytes written as a MAC address.

name: gNMI
discovers: Discover a host's interfaces and LLDP neighbors over gNMI (OpenConfig).
summary: Discover a host's interfaces and LLDP neighbors over gNMI (OpenConfig). Supports gnmi.

transports.name: gNMI
transports.description: Connects over gRPC; username and password travel as request metadata.

fields.label: gNMI Port
fields.help_text: 9339 is the IANA gNMI port; some NOSes listen on 6030 or 57400 instead.

fields.label: Username
fields.help_text: Sent as gRPC `username` metadata (the OpenConfig convention).

fields.label: Password
fields.help_text: Sent as gRPC `password` metadata.
